subject: Control plane identity handshake, fallback & migration plan

From: Alice Rogers <alice@acme-corp.com>

Cc: ACME SecOps <secops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Private control plane SSO + provisioning (ACME)

Hey Jordan —

Thanks for taking this with us. We want to confirm the onboarding path for our private control plane deployment: primary objectives are SAML SSO with signed assertions, SCIM v2 provisioning for users/groups, and a safe fallback cadence if SCIM push is unavailable. A few constraints from our side:

- All assertions must be signed and encrypted per our IdP policy.
- SCIM endpoint must be reachable only from a small set of IPs; we prefer an allowlist.
- We need detailed audit logs for every SCIM action (create/update/deactivate) for at least 1 year.
- If automated SCIM provisioning fails, we need a documented manual import (CSV) flow and temporary service-account-based uploads.

Attached is our current SCIM requirements doc and the security checklist. Can your team share a schematic of the handshake (metadata exchange, role mapping, service accounts) and the fallback approach? Also want to get a 60–90 minute walkthrough next week.

Alice Rogers
Director, Identity & SecOps
ACME Corporation

- acme_scim_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private control plane SSO + provisioning (ACME)

Hi Alice — great summary, thanks.

High-level handshake we propose (we can diagram during the call):
1) Metadata exchange: You send IdP metadata (SAML) to our private control plane config. We return SP metadata and the ACS/Entity IDs to your SAML admin.
2) Test IdP flow: We validate signed assertions against your certs with a staging tenant.
3) Role mapping: standard mapping of groups -> RBAC roles, with an "admin" override for emergency access.
4) SCIM provisioning: your IdP will POST to our SCIM endpoint over TLS; we accept SCIM v2 with the supplemental mapping fields (external_id -> account_id).
5) Fallback: If SCIM failures are detected, we (a) fire a webhook to ACME SecOps; (b) provide a pre-signed S3 import for CSV with a 1-hour TTL and (c) use a short-lived service account to apply imports.

Action items / proposed owners/dates:
- ACME: share SAML metadata + sample signed assertion (Alice) — by 2027-05-25
- Redwood infra: provide SP metadata + SCIM endpoint details (Marcus) — by 2027-05-24
- Security review: exception policy & audit retention confirmation (Mina) — by 2027-05-26
- Joint walkthrough (Zoom) — propose Tue 2027-05-25 10am PT

I attached our onboarding template to help collect required values.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private control plane SSO + provisioning (ACME) — technical notes

Jordan / Alice —

Couple of technical clarifications for the private control plane deployment (these will impact firewall and role design):

- SAML: we require NameID/email and an attribute called "groups" containing RFC 7644-compatible group IDs if you want group->role mapping. The SP will validate the signature and the NotOnOrAfter. Encrypted assertions are supported but add latency — we can support either.

- IAM roles: for private deployments we suggest a customer-managed role pattern. We'll need the role ARN(s) for the admin/developer/observer roles so we can seed the control plane RBAC mapping. If you prefer Redwood-managed roles, we can create them and hand over ARNs for your audit.

- SCIM push source IPs: the control plane will push provisioning events from our VPC egress IPs. For private control plane, SCIM traffic may flow over a VPC peering endpoint or a NAT gateway; end-to-end the requests originate from a deterministic CIDR block. Please allowlist the attached ranges.

- SCIM mapping specifics: we use externalId -> accountId; user.active -> active flag; and we currently do not map SSH keys (we can add hooks). Bulk import (CSV) needs the header: externalId,email,displayName,groups,status

- Token lifecycle: SCIM tokens are rotated every 30 days by default; we support a grace period for 2 rotations. A short-lived import service account will be issued with an expiry and logged.

Attaching the small text file with our SCIM push IP ranges. I'll post an updated runbook after the walkthrough.

Marcus Lin
Infra Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- scim_push_ip_ranges.txt (text/plain)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private control plane SSO + provisioning (ACME) — compliance notes

Team / Alice —

A couple of compliance-driven points to lock down before the walkthrough: 

- Audit logs: every SCIM operation (who, what, when, source IP, request id) must be immutable and retained for 12 months. We store logs in an append-only bucket and stream a subset to the customer's logging sink (if requested).

- KMS & key management: for private control plane we support CMKs from your KMS; we will sign artifacts with our envelope keys but can encrypt payloads with your key for storage-at-rest. Provide the KMS ARN if you want Redwood to use your key.

- CSV import exception: if the SCIM endpoint is blocked during cutover, we willenable a timeboxed manual import. To satisfy audit requirements we will: (a) require the import to be uploaded to a pre-signed S3 link that is versioned and write-once; (b) capture who triggered the import and attach the import request to the same audit trail; (c) rotate the service account used for the import and expire it within 2 hours.

- Fallback SLA: propose we commit to a 1-hour notification window for SCIM failures (alerts to ACME SecOps), and a 6-hour remediation window for automated retries. Manual import windows would be pre-scheduled with ACME for any planned maintenance.

Finally — Alice, please share the SOC2 report pointer if you need us to align controls; otherwise we'll provide our SOC2 evidence bundle for the integration.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
